cloudxr_web_client.operator_setup: Open the exact URL in the headset, select Isaac Lab, press Reset to defaults, then select the Quest 3 device profile before connecting.

preview.image_source: Isaac Lab Camera RGBA buffer reused for presentation; sensor exclusion is owned by the optional RTX Scene Partition integration, not buffer selection.
preview.implementation: upstream isaaclab_teleop XrCameraFeedSession and Kit SceneUI presenter
preview.panel_layout: Camera-resolution pixel layout; preserve upstream physical dimensions, labels and placement. Texture supersampling is 1.0.
preview.semantics: X changes upstream UiContainer visibility after one binding. Camera capture continues at configured simulation 30 Hz; hidden preview callbacks skip acquisition, staging and upload. Visible panels publish fresh camera frames at most 30 Hz through ByteImageProvider.set_raw_bytes_data with retained CPU uint8 RGBA buffers and on-demand SceneUI capture. Physics and renderer cadence are unchanged; panel visibility still requires physical Quest verification.

clutch.active_behavior: zero Cartesian delta while upstream continues updating its relative reference
clutch.release_behavior: discard the first released delta and rebase; no target jump

processor.disconnect: hold simulated targets, mark both streams inactive, and require per-arm rebase on reconnect; never replay stale intent

frames.arm_target: each Gate C base_link; both S1 base rotations are identity, so world spatial deltas have the same axes in each base
frames.upstream_transform: world_T_anchor uses [x, y, z]_isaac = [x, -z, y]_openxr before the configured anchor pose

gripper.mapping: aperture = open + normalized_trigger * (closed - open); trigger 0 is fully open and trigger 1 is fully closed; independent per arm

processor.reset: reset S1 environment and upstream execution state, then require one newly valid rebase frame per arm

rotation.target_composition: left-multiply spatial delta onto the current TCP orientation

sensitivity.mapping: Piecewise linear and clamped; left is slower, center keeps the previous normal speed, right is faster.
sensitivity.quest_control: each controller's own horizontal thumbstick axis

tracking.invalid: emit zero delta, hold simulated target, reject invalid/default or non-finite poses, invalidate that arm's relative reference and smoothing state, and leave the opposite valid arm usable
tracking.recovery: first newly valid pose becomes the new per-arm baseline and emits zero delta; subsequent samples resume without manual clutch
tracking.root_cause_remediation: TrackingSafeSe3RelRetargeter closes the pinned upstream Se3RelRetargeter is_none branch gap, which emitted zero but retained the stale previous wrist pose and smoothing accumulator
tracking.valid: controller present and grip_pose_valid with finite values

xr_presentation.rationale: Physical Quest evidence showed +1.20 m was far too low and -0.25 m was slightly too high. The selected VR anchor Z is now -0.10 m, lowering the unchanged table/robots by 0.15 m relative to the previous run; -90 degree world yaw still maps OpenXR forward to scene +X.

recenter.behavior: One rising edge uses XRCore.schedule_teleport_to_view so the current physical HMD pose matches the validated demo scene-camera pose; controller poses use XRCore's full physical-to-virtual transform including the resulting space origin, while robot/table USD geometry and 1:1 scale remain unchanged.
recenter.motion_barrier: Hold the request frame; on the next control frame accept XRCore's current physical-to-world transform as the new reference and emit a zero-motion rebase. Any later transform change rebases again. Missing active XR transforms still hold motion.
